title: A Message That Needed One More Detail

source.rights: 原创 AI 辅助虚构教学材料，尚待发布前独立审核。

instructions: Read the passage and choose one answer for each question.
passage:
Sofia and Ben are preparing a small discussion evening at a community center. On Monday, Sofia sends Ben a message: “We need the room on Thursday.” The sentence gives a day, but it does not give a time. Ben assumes that the event is in the morning, because another group usually meets there then. Sofia thinks he knows that she means five in the afternoon. Neither person has checked the other's idea.

On Tuesday, Ben sees that the room is already booked in the morning. His first response is to write “This is urgent!” in a message to Sofia. He wants to explain the problem quickly, but he does not mention the morning booking. Sofia reads the word “urgent” and feels upset because she thinks the whole event must be canceled. She waits until she has a quiet moment to reply. Instead of guessing again, she suggests a short conversation after lunch.

When they meet, Sofia asks Ben to describe what he found. She tries to listen without interrupting. Ben says that he was looking at the morning booking. Sofia explains that her plan is for five in the afternoon. “I should have included the time,” she says. “I apologize for the confusion.” Ben also apologizes because his message did not say which booking worried him. They agree to check the room schedule together. To clarify the plan, Sofia asks whether Ben can suggest another time if five is unavailable. They will discuss a backup with the manager rather than change the event without asking the group. Their aim is to keep all participants informed.

The room is free after four, so they can use it at five. Ben offers to send a polite request to the center manager. He wants to communicate both the day and the time. Sofia suggests a phrase: “Could you tell me whether the room is available at five on Thursday?” Ben likes the purpose of the question: it asks for confirmation without assuming the manager has made a mistake. They decide not to make the message more formal than necessary, because they know the manager well.

Before sending it, Ben reads the message aloud. Sofia notices that the tone sounds calm. She asks him to repeat the time once, and they compare it with the booking page. The manager later confirms that the room is available. In her opinion, the extra detail is helpful, and she asks them to remind her on Wednesday. Ben and Sofia write a short note after the exchange: if a message seems unclear, ask a question before deciding what the other person meant. Their dialogue does not mean that every misunderstanding has one simple reason, but this time a clear choice of words helped.
